*Written by: Nimesh Chakravarthi, Co-founder & CTO, Struct*


## Why Struct Beats Swimlane SOAR for 2026 Engineering Teams


- Legacy SOAR platforms like Swimlane depend on brittle playbooks that cap automated coverage near 30% and drain Seed-to-Series-C engineering capacity.
- Agentic AI investigation platforms reason over evidence at runtime and deliver complete root cause analysis in under 5 minutes.
- Modern automated investigation tools now provide zero-click root cause analysis, blast-radius quantification, conversational Slack follow-up, custom runbook execution, and clean handoff to code fixes.
- Struct cuts triage time by roughly 80% with a 10-minute deployment, while legacy SOAR platforms such as Swimlane and Cortex XSOAR often need many months to mature.
- Struct automates on-call investigations so teams remove manual investigation tax and let junior engineers handle incidents safely.


## The Problem: Why Swimlane SOAR Playbooks Slow Investigations


Legacy SOAR platforms rest on a simple premise: encode every investigative path as a deterministic if-then playbook. That premise breaks down at scale.[In production, most SOAR programs cap out at roughly 30% of alert types before playbook maintenance consumes the savings](https://d3security.com/blog/soar-is-costing-more-than-you-think/) , with the playbook library covering only the most common incident types. The remaining alerts land back in the analyst queue.


The maintenance burden is structural, not vendor-specific. SOC teams managing numerous playbooks spend substantial time each year on manual playbook authoring, testing, versioning, and redeployment. They also spend a significant portion of SOC engineering time keeping integrations alive as the tool stack evolves. Repairing a single broken integration often requires substantial engineering time, during which the integration sits dark and the coverage it powered goes quiet. These integration failures are symptoms of a deeper structural issue: the implementation model itself.


[Legacy SOAR platforms often involve long implementations with static playbooks and custom scripting](https://torq.io/blog/soar-replacement-2026) . The engineers who build those playbooks encode tribal knowledge that evaporates when they leave.[The FTE engineer dedicated to SOAR playbook maintenance produces zero direct security value, turning the platform into legacy technical debt.](https://prophetsecurity.ai/blog/soar-alternative-why-ai-soc-analysts-are-replacing-static-playbooks) For fast-growing software engineering teams at Seed-to-Series-C companies, this model does not scale.


[Teams running many playbooks spend significant time on maintenance alone, and that number grows every time the environment changes.](https://strike48.com/post/soar-alternative) A large portion of alerts in legacy SOAR environments go uninvestigated. The result is predictable: alert backlogs, SLA breaches, and senior engineers pulled away from product development to fight fires that an automated system should resolve.

## The Solution: What Agentic AI Investigation Platforms Replace


Agentic AI investigation platforms act as autonomous reasoning engines that correlate logs, metrics, traces, and code context at runtime, without static if-then logic.[AI agents correlate data across the engineering and security stack in seconds rather than waiting for sequential playbook steps or human handoffs between tiers.](https://prophetsecurity.ai/blog/soar-alternative-why-ai-soc-analysts-are-replacing-static-playbooks) They investigate every alert immediately and in parallel, with no queue wait time and no playbook to author or maintain.


[Agentic AI enables autonomous agents to plan and execute response actions across multiple steps, reason about goals, select tools, and adapt to unexpected conditions within guardrails.](https://vectra.ai/topics/incident-response-automation) These systems close the majority of Tier-1 alerts without human help. Gartner retired the SOAR Magic Quadrant in 2025, reflecting this shift toward agentic investigation and response.


## Key Capabilities of Automated Investigation Tools for Engineering Teams


Modern agentic investigation platforms replace legacy SOAR functions with capabilities that require no ongoing engineering maintenance:


- **Zero-click root cause analysis:** The platform automatically triggers an investigation the moment an alert fires, correlating logs, traces, metrics, and code exceptions into a unified timeline before a human is paged.
- **Blast-radius quantification:** The system instantly assesses user and service impact and surfaces that context directly in the engineer’s communication channel (Slack, PagerDuty) without manual cross-referencing.
- **Conversational follow-up:** Engineers interact with the AI in Slack to test hypotheses, pull additional log windows, or verify impact on specific users, all within the alert thread.
- **Custom runbook encoding:** Teams input their existing on-call runbooks, correlation ID formats, and investigation procedures. The AI follows those procedures on every alert and removes tribal-knowledge risk.
- **Seamless handoff:** Once root cause is confirmed, the platform hands context to a coding agent or generates a pull request, closing the loop from alert detection to code resolution.


These capabilities work best when paired with high-fidelity alerting. Signature-based detection typically achieves lower false positive rates (under 1%) than anomaly-based or ML behavioral detection (3–5%), which keeps engineers focused on genuine incidents instead of noise.


## Manual vs. Assisted vs. Fully Automated Triage


**Manual triage** requires an engineer to acknowledge the alert, open multiple observability platforms, manually correlate logs and traces, cross-reference code changes in GitHub, and determine root cause.[An average enterprise SOC receives around 4,300 alerts daily, with analysts typically spending 20–40 minutes investigating each alert manually.](https://www.crogl.com/resources/press/new-research-report) At that rate, alert backlogs become inevitable.


**Assisted triage** with legacy SOAR automates the most common playbook paths but demands ongoing engineering to maintain those paths. Triage time can drop significantly with modern platforms, yet only for alerts that match an existing playbook. Novel alerts still revert to manual handling.


**Fully automated triage** with agentic AI investigates every alert end-to-end at runtime, even when the pattern is new.[Agentic AI SOC analysts can handle multiple concurrent investigations without performance degradation and learn from past incidents to refine future actions.](https://intezer.com/guides/ai-soc) For software engineering teams, the investigation often finishes before the on-call engineer opens their laptop.


## How Agentic Investigation Tools Plug into SIEM, EDR, and Observability


Agentic investigation platforms integrate as active participants in the existing stack rather than replacements.[The agent orchestrates workflows across disparate systems such as SIEM, threat intelligence feeds, cloud security platforms, and EDR solutions to enrich alerts, retrieve endpoint telemetry, and look up asset context.](https://stellarcyber.ai/learn/agentic-ai-security)


For software engineering teams, the integration surface maps directly to the modern observability stack. Alert triggers come from Slack, PagerDuty, or Linear. Log and metrics context flows from Datadog, AWS CloudWatch, GCP Logs, Azure, Grafana, Prometheus, or Sumo Logic. Exception context arrives from Sentry, and code context from GitHub.[Strong integrations let agentic AI move from recommendation to execution, while weak integrations confine the system to passive outputs.](https://cymulate.com/cybersecurity-glossary/agentic-ai-in-cybersecurity)


Several prerequisites support a successful deployment. Basic logging and trace IDs must already exist in the stack. Alerting triggers must be configured in a designated channel. The team should define which alert types require human approval before automated action.[Starting with high-volume, low-risk scenarios before tackling anything irreversible remains a core best practice for incident response automation programs.](https://vectra.ai/topics/incident-response-automation)


## Implementation Stages for a 10-Minute Struct Pilot


1. **Connect your issue source (2 minutes):** Authenticate Slack or PagerDuty and designate the alert channels Struct should monitor.
2. **Connect your code repository (2 minutes):** Authenticate GitHub so the platform can correlate recent commits and code changes with active alerts.
3. **Connect your observability stack (4 minutes):** Authenticate Datadog, AWS CloudWatch, GCP Logs, Sentry, or equivalent tools. Struct begins querying these sources automatically on the next alert.
4. **Encode your runbook (optional, ongoing):** Paste your existing on-call runbook into Struct’s custom instructions. The AI follows your team’s exact operational procedures on every investigation.
5. **First automated investigation:** The next alert that fires triggers a full automated investigation. By the time the on-call engineer is paged, the root cause, blast radius, and suggested fix already appear in Slack.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### How does workflow automation in agentic AI differ from traditional SOAR playbook automation?


Traditional SOAR automation executes predefined if-then logic: if field A equals value B, run action C. Every investigative path must be manually authored, tested, and maintained by an engineer. Agentic AI automation reasons through evidence at runtime, selects tools, and adapts its investigation path based on what it finds, without a pre-authored playbook. This means agentic platforms investigate novel alerts that SOAR platforms would escalate to humans by default, and they avoid ongoing playbook maintenance as the environment changes. For software engineering teams, agentic AI delivers a complete root cause analysis before the on-call engineer is paged instead of routing the alert to a human because no matching playbook exists.


### What gaps does agentic AI fill that SIEM alone cannot address?


SIEM platforms aggregate and correlate log data and surface alerts, but they do not investigate those alerts autonomously. A SIEM tells an engineer that something happened. An agentic investigation platform tells the engineer what happened, why it happened, which users or services are affected, and what to do next. The investigation step, which includes correlating logs, mapping a timeline, cross-referencing code changes, and quantifying blast radius, remains manual with SIEM alone. Agentic AI automates that entire investigation step and compresses 30–45 minutes of manual work into a 5-minute automated report delivered directly in Slack.


### What data quality requirements must be in place before deploying an agentic investigation platform?


Agentic investigation platforms reason over the telemetry data available in the connected stack. The minimum viable prerequisites include structured logs with consistent trace or correlation IDs, at least one observability platform (Datadog, AWS CloudWatch, GCP Logs, or equivalent) actively ingesting application telemetry, an exception tracking tool such as Sentry, and an alerting trigger configured in a designated Slack channel or ticketing system. Teams with malformed logs, no trace IDs, or no active alerting configuration will not get accurate root cause analysis from any platform in this category. If the observability foundation is missing, that investment should precede agentic AI deployment. Struct is purpose-built for software engineering teams already using tools like Sentry, Datadog or cloud logs, and Slack for alerts, which forms a strong baseline for immediate value.


### Should engineering teams build their own automated investigation tooling or buy a purpose-built platform?


Building a custom automated investigation system requires engineering resources to integrate with every observability tool, maintain those integrations as APIs change, build a reasoning layer capable of correlating multi-source telemetry, and keep the system current as the stack evolves. This mirrors the same maintenance tax that makes legacy SOAR platforms expensive, except the cost lands entirely on the engineering team rather than a vendor. For Seed-to-Series-C software engineering companies, the build path diverts senior engineering time from product development to reliability infrastructure, which automated investigation is meant to relieve. Purpose-built platforms like Struct deploy in 10 minutes, include SOC 2 and HIPAA compliance out of the box, and let teams encode their specific runbooks without writing or maintaining integration code. The build option makes sense mainly for organizations with unique compliance requirements that mandate full on-premise deployment and dedicated platform engineering headcount.


## Conclusion: Trade-offs and Next Steps


Legacy SOAR platforms like Swimlane still deliver value for organizations with dedicated playbook engineers, stable tool stacks, and the runway to absorb long implementation cycles. For Seed-to-Series-C software engineering teams, those conditions rarely exist. The playbook maintenance tax compounds faster than automation savings, alert coverage stalls below meaningful levels, and the tribal-knowledge dependency on the engineer who built the playbooks creates organizational fragility.


Agentic AI investigation platforms remove the maintenance tax by reasoning through evidence at runtime. The main trade-off is data quality dependency, because these platforms are only as accurate as the telemetry they can access. Teams with mature observability stacks see immediate, measurable MTTR reduction. Teams without structured logging need to address that foundation first.
